1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Orvanta Play is a fictional subscription video service operating in eleven markets. In October its smaller market, Kestria (about 400,000 subscribers), moved video delivery from its long-standing CDN provider, Corvane Edge, to a new provider, Tessaline Networks. Since then, buffering complaints in Kestria have risen sharply while every other market is stable. The regional VP blames the new CDN and wants to penalise the vendor and switch back.
9	Your request: From the CTO, 16 November: 'Before Thursday's leadership meeting I need a clear view of what is behind the Kestria buffering and whether we should approve Mireille's plan: SLA breach notice to Tessaline, October fees withheld, traffic moved back to Corvane. Tell me what is going on and what we should do next.'
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Customer support ticketing system export (system-record): Ticketing system export, tag 'buffering/playback', market = Kestria. Weekly ticket counts: 22–28 Sep 118; 29 Sep–5 Oct 124; 6–12 Oct 433; 13–19 Oct 641; 20–26 Oct 628; 27 Oct–2 Nov 655; 3–9 Nov 637. Rate per 10,000 subscribers: 3.1 before 6 Oct, 16.0–16.4 from mid-October onward. All other markets combined: 2.8–3.2 per 10,000 every week, no trend. The device field on the ticket form is optional and is blank on 71% of Kestria tickets.
12	- Change management system, CHG-4471 (change-record): CHG-4471 — Kestria CDN provider migration. Scope: all Orvanta Play video delivery for Kestria (all apps, all ISPs) moved from Corvane Edge to Tessaline Networks, served from Tessaline's Varsk point of presence. Cutover: DNS weights shifted gradually from 8 Oct 22:00 to 9 Oct 04:10 local time; 100% of Kestria traffic on Tessaline from 04:10 on 9 Oct. Rollback: revert DNS weights, estimated 2 hours; Corvane contract for Kestria ends 31 Dec. All other markets remain on Corvane; no further migrations planned before 2027. Status: closed — successful, no errors during cutover.
13	- Playback quality dashboard (country view) (telemetry): Playback quality dashboard, country level. Daily rebuffering ratio (share of viewing time spent stalled), Kestria: 5 Oct 0.6%; 6 Oct 0.6%; 7 Oct 0.5%; 8 Oct 0.6%; 9 Oct 1.7%; 10 Oct 2.7%; 11 Oct 2.7%; 12–31 Oct 2.6–2.9%; 1–15 Nov 2.7–2.9%. Handball match nights (11, 18, 25 Oct): 2.7%, 2.8%, 2.7%. All other markets: 0.5–0.7% every day. Annotation, 11 Oct: 'Kestrian Handball League streaming launch; Kestria viewing hours +21% week on week.' The dashboard offers no breakdown below country level.
14	- Email from Mireille Okonta-Haas, VP Kestria, to the CTO and Head of Partnerships, 3 November (leadership-account): 'Since we moved Kestria to Tessaline on 8 October our buffering complaints have gone up fivefold, and nothing else in the region changed. Every other market is still on Corvane and is fine. October cancellations hit 3.4% of the base against 2.1% in September. Yes, the 1 October price rise was always going to cost us something, but this is the network. I want an SLA breach notice sent to Tessaline this week, their October fees withheld, and Kestria back on Corvane before that contract lapses. Also, please silence the Kestria rebuffering alert in the ops channel. We know the cause and it is paging people every night.'
15	- Product release digest, week 41, compiled by Product Operations (document): Release digest, week 41. 'Orvanta Play for smart TVs 5.2 is live in all markets as of 9 October (store listings approved 8 October). Highlights: redesigned home rails, 12% fewer crashes in beta, faster video start. Beta feedback positive. No playback regressions reported from any market. Mobile and web apps: no releases this sprint; next mobile release planned for December.'
16	- Call notes, Tobiah Lenn, senior network engineer, 14 October (staff-account): Notes from call with Tobiah Lenn. 'Tessaline's Varsk cache was cold after cutover. Their portal showed a hit ratio around 88% in the first week, against roughly 95% from Corvane. Our synthetic probes show p95 segment fetch time went from about 180 ms to about 215 ms. That is the kind of shift that tips players into stalls at peak time. I would put money on the CDN. The handball launch added load too, but the stalls started two days before that.'
17	
18	BRIEF:
19	The Kestria buffering problem is almost certainly not the new CDN. Telemetry for 12–25 October shows that only the smart-TV app version 5.2 stalls badly: 5.9% rebuffering, against 0.6–0.7% for every other client. That holds on all three ISPs. Web, mobile and older-version TV sessions are also served by Tessaline, and they are normal. Version 5.2 went live on 9 October, the same day as the CDN cutover, so the two changes were confounded until this breakdown separated them. The handball launch came after the problem began, and match nights are no worse. ISP congestion is ruled out because the same ISPs are fine for other clients.
20	
21	Recommendation: do not send the breach notice, withhold fees or roll back to Corvane. Do not mute the alert. Instead, revert 5.2's adaptive-streaming behaviour for Kestria, or pause the rollout, and have the TV team fix the regression. Check the 5.2 rollout settings to confirm. Hold the free-month offer. The October price rise also affects cancellations, and the link between buffering and cancellations is unproven. Add app-version breakdowns to the dashboard. I am fairly confident in this diagnosis. The cancellation question is still open.
22
